title: Multiplication as equal groups
examples: Is multiplication the same as adding?
What does the times sign mean?

explain.say: Picture 4 plates at a party in Lagos, and each plate has 3 puff-puffs, little sweet doughnuts. How many puff-puffs? Look at the board: 4 groups, with 3 in each group. That makes 12.
Look at just 2 plates first. 2 groups of 3 means 3 and 3, which is 6. Every plate has the same number, so the groups are equal. Is every plate the same?
Now all 4 plates: 3, 6, 9, 12. Adding the same number again and again is called repeated addition. We write 4 times 3 equals 12. The times sign means groups of. Can you say it with me?
What if there are 3 plates with 4 on each? 4, 8, 12. Also 12! But the picture looks different: fewer groups, more in each. Which way would you lay the table?
Well done! Multiplying is a fast way to add equal groups. A baker in Paris fills 6 boxes with 5 croissants each: 6 times 5 is 30. Challenge: how many legs do 3 cats have?

faq.a: It means 4 groups that each have 3 things. Add them up: 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3 is 12, so 4 groups of 3 is 12.

faq.q: Is multiplication the same as adding?
faq.a: Multiplication is a fast way of adding equal groups. 4 times 3 gives the same answer as 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3, just quicker.

faq.q: What does the times sign mean?
faq.a: The times sign means groups of, or lots of. 4 times 3 can be read as 4 groups of 3.
asks: What does the multiply sign mean?

faq.q: Why must the groups be equal?
faq.a: Multiplying only works when every group has the same number. If one plate had 5 and the others had 3, you would need to add them instead.
asks: What if the groups are different sizes?

faq.q: How many legs do 3 cats have?
faq.a: Each cat has 4 legs, so 3 groups of 4 is 4, 8, 12. That is 12 legs.

facts: The × sign for multiplication was first printed by the English mathematician William Oughtred in 1631.

quiz.say: Which sum means the same as 3 times 6?
quiz.show: Which sum means the same as 3 × 6?
quiz.why: 3 groups of 6 is 6 plus 6 plus 6, which is 18.
